key_insight: Materials GNNs can achieve similar final accuracy with very different amounts of trainable parameter-space freedom, so intrinsic dimensionality reveals a hidden measure of model dependence beyond endpoint error.
engineering_relevance: Random-subspace intrinsic-dimension analysis offers a practical stress test for choosing architectures and sizing models when robustness to reduced optimization capacity matters in materials property prediction.
method: Train CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DimeNet++ inside randomly oriented low-dimensional parameter subspaces.
Track recovery curves as more trainable degrees of freedom are restored.
Compare six prediction tasks plus dataset-size and width sweeps to separate accuracy from dimensional demand.
evidence_signal: Across six tasks, the authors report that metallic classification and log-bulk-modulus regression recover near-reference performance from small fractional subspaces, while phonon prediction is the most sensitive to dimensional restriction.
watch_item: Random-subspace results depend on the chosen architecture, task, and training setup, so threshold dimensions should be interpreted as comparative diagnostics rather than universal constants.
paper_title: Measuring trainable degrees of freedom in materials graph neural networks: a random-subspace intrinsic dimension analysis
